nba9530bc70d.s: Which one of the following is correct about the United Kingdom's constitutional system?
o: It was formed by a compact among States.
Parliament holds all law-making power, reflecting its unitary character.
Residual powers are divided between the centre and the provinces.
The judiciary distributes legislative subjects among the units.
nba9530bc70d.x: The United Kingdom is a unitary country in which Parliament holds all law-making power.

nd90a2c44e7a.s: Federalism is a system in which:
o: all power is concentrated in one central authority
the Union and States share power, each supreme in its own sphere under a written Constitution
sovereign States form a loose league with a right to secede
local units exercise only powers delegated by the Centre
nd90a2c44e7a.x: Federalism divides powers constitutionally between the Union and the States, each supreme in its own sphere, with an independent umpire to settle disputes.

nde492e6e8a0.s: An independent judiciary acting as umpire in Union-State disputes is regarded as:
o: a unitary feature of the Constitution
a feature of a confederation
an essential feature of federalism
a Directive Principle of State Policy
nde492e6e8a0.x: An independent judiciary can act as an impartial umpire in Centre-State disputes, which is regarded as an essential feature of federalism.

n406a8e51237.s: In Kesavananda Bharati (1973), the federal character of the Constitution was held to be:
o: outside the basic structure
one of the basic features of the Constitution
applicable only in normal times
confined to the Seventh Schedule
n406a8e51237.x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) listed the federal character among the basic features of the Constitution.

n39f6ebd2306.s: The Supreme Court has described the Indian Constitution as:
o: purely federal with no unitary features
fundamentally federal with pronounced unitary elements
confederal, with sovereign States
purely unitary with a nominal federal distribution
n39f6ebd2306.x: The Constitution has been described as fundamentally federal with pronounced unitary elements, reflecting a federal distribution alongside strong centralising provisions.

nindian-polity-51-15.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Judicial review is a unitary element of the Constitution.
2. Judicial review reinforces the federal principle.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
nindian-polity-51-15.x: Judicial review supports federalism by upholding the division of powers; it is not a unitary feature like emergency provisions or All India Services.

nc35d5076d4b.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a confederation from a federation?
o: A federation needs no written division of powers.
A federation is a temporary league of sovereign States.
A confederation always has a stronger centre than a federation.
A confederation is made of sovereign States that retain the right to secede.
nc35d5076d4b.x: A confederation is a loose league of sovereign States that generally keep the right to secede, while a federation creates a constitutional division of powers.

n04284562aea.s: How does the origin of Indian federalism differ from that of the USA?
o: The USA was first unitary; India was formed by an agreement among States
The USA was formed by integration of States; India moved from a unitary colonial system to a federal one
Both arose from the break-up of unitary systems
Both were created by amendments made by their central governments
n04284562aea.x: The US federation was formed by agreement and integration of States, while India converted a unitary colonial set-up into a federal one, giving it a centripetal bias.

n1d8763a0142.s: A law made under Articles 3 and 4 that alters the First and Fourth Schedules is:
o: deemed an amendment under Article 368
valid only if passed by a special majority
not deemed an amendment under Article 368
valid only after ratification by half the States
n1d8763a0142.x: Article 4 permits consequential changes in the First and Fourth Schedules, and such a law is not deemed an amendment of the Constitution under Article 368.

n1f188e26b7a.s: According to Dr B.R. Ambedkar, the use of the word 'Union' shows that:
o: the Union was formed by a compact of sovereign States
India is not the result of an agreement among States, and States cannot secede
the States retain a right to secede
the Constitution is set in a tight mould of federalism
n1f188e26b7a.x: Ambedkar stressed that India was not formed by an agreement among States, that States had no right to secede, and that the system could be unitary or federal as circumstances required.

n72f6d5319dd.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 371 – Mizoram
Article 371A – Goa
Article 371D – Andhra Pradesh
Article 371J – Sikkim
n72f6d5319dd.x: Article 371D gives special provisions for Andhra Pradesh. Article 371 covers Maharashtra and Gujarat, 371A Nagaland, and 371J Karnataka (Sikkim is 371F).

n97e788ef497.s: Which one of the following is correct regarding State constitutions in India and the USA?
o: Every Indian State has its own constitution; no US State has one
Both Indian and US States have their own constitutions
Neither Indian nor US States have separate constitutions
Indian States generally have no separate constitutions; each US State has its own
n97e788ef497.x: Indian States generally do not have separate constitutions (the former Jammu and Kashmir was an exception), while each US State has its own.

nindian-polity-68-18.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Economic and social planning is a Union List subject.
2. Corporation tax is a Union List subject, while land revenue is a State List subject.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
nindian-polity-68-18.x: Corporation tax is in the Union List and land revenue in the State List; economic and social planning is Concurrent List Entry 20, so statement 1 is wrong.

nindian-polity-68-29.s: Which of the following was NOT transferred to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976?
o: Administration of justice
Weights and measures
Public order
Protection of wild animals and birds
nindian-polity-68-29.x: Public order remained in the State List (Entry 1). The 42nd Amendment moved education, forests, weights and measures, protection of wild animals and birds, and administration of justice.

nindian-polity-68-43.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Tolls and capitation taxes – State List
Inter-State migration and quarantine – Union List
Local government and Panchayati Raj – State List
Public health and sanitation – Concurrent List
nindian-polity-68-43.x: Public health and sanitation is a State List subject, not Concurrent. The other three pairs are correct.

nd46c48a0658.s: Which one of the following about the use of Concurrent List entries is correct?
o: Entry 33 concerns only the organisation of the Supreme Court and High Courts.
The Union has used them for farm laws (Entry 33) and education measures such as the NEP and NMC Act.
Only State Legislatures can legislate on Concurrent subjects.
The Concurrent List bars Union laws on education.
nd46c48a0658.x: Concurrent List entries permit Union legislation; cited examples include farm laws through Entry 33 and education measures such as the NEP and NMC Act.

n1ed4fbc1391.s: Which of the following correctly states where residuary powers lie?
o: India and Canada – States; USA – Centre
India – Governor-General; Canada – States
India and Canada – Centre; USA and Australia – States
India, Canada, USA and Australia – all with the Centre
n1ed4fbc1391.x: Residuary powers lie with the Centre in India and Canada, and with the States in the USA and Australia; under the 1935 Act they were vested in the Governor-General.

n95c60d6c521.s: Elections to State Legislatures and elections conducted by the Election Commission fall respectively under:
o: Union Entry 37 and State Entry 72
State Entry 37 and Union Entry 72
Concurrent Entry 25 and Union Entry 64
State Entry 50 and Concurrent Entry 20
n95c60d6c521.x: Elections to the State Legislature are State List Entry 37 (subject to parliamentary law); elections conducted by the Election Commission are Union List Entry 72.

nindian-polity-50-2.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 356 – Threat to the financial stability of India
Article 360 – Failure of constitutional machinery in a State
Article 352 – Failure of constitutional machinery in a State
Article 352 – War, external aggression or armed rebellion
nindian-polity-50-2.x: Article 352 covers war, external aggression or armed rebellion; Article 356 covers failure of constitutional machinery in a State; Article 360 covers a threat to financial stability.

nindian-polity-50-25.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: National Emergency – six months at a time, up to three years
President's Rule – six months at a time, up to three years
Financial Emergency – six months at a time, up to three years
President's Rule – six months at a time, with no maximum limit
nindian-polity-50-25.x: President's Rule continues six months at a time up to three years; a National Emergency has no maximum limit, and a Financial Emergency once approved continues until revoked.

n2a400982fda.s: Which of the following is NOT a financial consequence of a National Emergency?
o: Transfers to States may be reduced or cancelled, subject to Parliament's approval
An obligatory increase in transfers of funds to States
The President may modify the distribution of revenues between the Union and States
The Union may issue directions affecting its financial relations with States
n2a400982fda.x: The President may modify revenue distribution and reduce or cancel transfers to States; an increase in transfers is not a specified consequence.

nindian-polity-50-48.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. President's Rule does not directly suspend Fundamental Rights.
2. A Financial Emergency does not directly suspend Fundamental Rights.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
nindian-polity-50-48.x: Only a National Emergency affects Fundamental Rights (Articles 358 and 359); President's Rule and a Financial Emergency do not suspend them directly.

n0a4b7d44ed6.s: Under Article 255, an Act passed without the required previous sanction but later assented to by the Governor or President is:
o: void from the beginning
valid only after re-enactment
not invalid merely for want of that sanction
valid only if upheld by the Supreme Court
n0a4b7d44ed6.x: Article 255 treats the recommendation or previous sanction as procedural; subsequent assent prevents invalidity on that ground alone.

nefd1d111edb.s: A State law on a State List subject conflicts with a valid Parliamentary law under the Concurrent List. Which ordinarily prevails?
o: The State law
The later of the two laws
The Parliamentary law
The law approved by the Governor
nefd1d111edb.x: The Concurrent List has precedence over the State List, so a valid Parliamentary law on a Concurrent matter ordinarily prevails over an inconsistent State law.

n8740cce5804.s: A State Bill imposing reasonable restrictions on inter-State trade in the public interest requires the previous sanction of the:
o: Governor
Rajya Sabha
Inter-State Council
President
n8740cce5804.x: A State may impose reasonable restrictions on inter-State trade in the public interest, but such a Bill needs the President's previous sanction.

n0c7c6fd984f.s: Under Article 251, if a Parliamentary law made under Article 249 or 250 conflicts with a State law:
o: the Governor decides which prevails
the Parliamentary law prevails
the State law prevails
both laws become void to the extent of conflict
n0c7c6fd984f.x: Article 251 provides that a Parliamentary law made under Article 249 or 250 prevails over an inconsistent State law.

n82f814b8d04.s: While an Article 249 resolution is in force, the State Legislature:
o: may legislate only with the Rajya Sabha's consent
loses its power, which passes to the Governor
may still legislate, but the Parliamentary law prevails in a conflict
stands dissolved for the duration of the resolution
n82f814b8d04.x: An Article 249 resolution does not suspend the State Legislature's power, but the Parliamentary law prevails if the two conflict.

nindian-polity-68-19.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Panchayati Raj and Municipalities are in the Union List.
2. Article 246A empowers both Parliament and State Legislatures to make GST laws.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
nindian-polity-68-19.x: Article 246A gives both Parliament and State Legislatures power over GST; Panchayati Raj and Municipalities are State List subjects (Entry 5).

n7d399f145ba.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched regarding Parliament's power to legislate on State List matters?
o: Article 249 – National interest
Article 250 – Proclamation of Emergency
Article 356 – President's Rule in a State
Article 252 – Request by a single State Legislature
n7d399f145ba.x: Article 252 needs resolutions from the legislatures of two or more States, not one State alone. The other pairs are correct.

nd0eb72fa667.s: Parliament can legislate on a State List subject to implement an international convention under:
o: Article 249
Article 356
Article 253
Article 250
nd0eb72fa667.x: Article 253 empowers Parliament to make laws implementing treaties, agreements and conventions, even on State List subjects.

n2f89acafa00.s: Regulations having the force of Acts of Parliament for Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep are made by the:
o: Lieutenant Governor
President
Union Home Minister
Chief Secretary of the Union Territory
n2f89acafa00.x: Regulations made by the President for Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep have the force and effect of an Act of Parliament.

nindian-polity-68-7.s: Which of the following is INCORRECT about repugnancy on Concurrent List subjects?
o: In a conflict, the Central law generally prevails.
Repugnancy is dealt with under Article 250.
The Central-law rule has an exception relating to Presidential assent.
A reserved State law that gets Presidential assent may prevail under Article 254(2).
nindian-polity-68-7.x: Repugnancy on Concurrent subjects is dealt with by Article 254, not Article 250 (Emergency legislation).

nb2f85a20b0d.s: Which case upheld a State prohibition law under the doctrine of pith and substance?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Prafulla Kumar Mukherjee v. Bank of Commerce
State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara
K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo v. State of Orissa
nb2f85a20b0d.x: In State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara (1951), the prohibition law was upheld under pith and substance; its incidental encroachment did not change its true character.

nindian-polity-2-50.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Articles 256 to 263 deal with administrative relations.
2. Article 263 deals with the Inter-State Council.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
nindian-polity-2-50.x: Articles 256-263 cover administrative relations, ending with Article 263 on the Inter-State Council.

nindian-polity-2-51.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Articles 268 to 281 deal with the distribution of revenues.
2. Article 281 deals with the recommendations of the Finance Commission.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
nindian-polity-2-51.x: Articles 268-281 deal with distribution of revenues, ending with Article 281 on the Finance Commission's recommendations (the Commission itself is Article 280).

nindian-polity-67-4.s: What is the effect of the Doctrine of Severability?
o: The whole statute is declared void
Only the unconstitutional part is declared void, if separable
A law is tested only by its title
Parliament must re-enact the entire law
nindian-polity-67-4.x: Under severability, only the unconstitutional part of a law is struck down if it can be separated; the rest survives.

n8fe80c73dbb.s: The Union List and Concurrent List originally had 97 and 47 subjects. How many do they have today?
o: 97 and 52
98 and 52
98 and 47
n8fe80c73dbb.x: The Union List now has 98 subjects (97 originally) and the Concurrent List 52 (47 originally).

nindian-polity-68-24.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Defence and armed forces – Union List
Public order – State List
Education – Union List
Space research – Residuary subject under Article 248
nindian-polity-68-24.x: Education is a Concurrent List subject, not Union List. Defence is Union, public order is State (Entry 1), and space research is residuary under Article 248.

n7679943c96c.s: In Scheduled Areas, who may bar or modify the application of Acts of Parliament?
o: The State Legislature
The Chief Minister
The Tribes Advisory Council
The Governor
n7679943c96c.x: The Governor may bar or modify the application of Acts of Parliament in Scheduled Areas.

nde070d0a7a5.s: In a Union Territory, executive power is ordinarily exercised by the:
o: Chief Secretary of the Union Territory
Union Home Minister in every matter
Lieutenant Governor or Administrator, as the President's representative
elected municipal council alone
nde070d0a7a5.x: The Lieutenant Governor or Administrator exercises executive power in a Union Territory as the President's representative.

nindian-polity-8-34.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The President holds Rank 1 in the Order of Precedence.
2. The President is the Head of the State, not the Head of the Government.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
nindian-polity-8-34.x: The President is first in the Order of Precedence and is Head of State, while the Prime Minister heads the Government.

n5158d33693b.s: Executive power over Concurrent List subjects ordinarily rests with:
o: the Union exclusively
the States, subject to constitutional or statutory exceptions
the President and Governor jointly
local governments exclusively
n5158d33693b.x: By default, executive power over Concurrent subjects stays with the States; the Centre exercises it only where the Constitution or a Parliamentary law expressly provides.

n71adeeef80c.s: How does Article 258(2) differ from Article 258(1)?
o: It applies only during a National Emergency
It concerns inter-State agreements on river-valley projects
It lets the Governor transfer State functions to the Union
It lets Parliament by law confer duties on State officers without State consent
n71adeeef80c.x: Under Article 258(2), Parliament may by law confer powers or duties on State officers without State consent; Article 258(1) involves Presidential entrustment with State consent.

n855c942247c.s: Under Article 353, what is the effect of a National Emergency on executive relations?
o: The Union may direct States on any matter, but State governments are not suspended
State governments are suspended and replaced by administrators
The State Council of Ministers is dismissed in every State
The powers of the High Courts pass to the Union executive
n855c942247c.x: During a National Emergency the Union's power of direction expands under Article 353, but State governments continue and are not suspended.

n2008b52f71a.s: Which of the following is a possible effect of a Financial Emergency under Article 360?
o: State Legislatures stand dissolved
Fundamental Rights are directly suspended
State Money and Financial Bills may be reserved for the President
The Union automatically assumes all State legislative powers
n2008b52f71a.x: During a Financial Emergency, the Centre may require Money Bills and other Financial Bills of States to be reserved for the President's consideration.

nf6b10dca97d.s:
Under Article 239AA, which of the following are outside the legislative competence of the Delhi Legislative Assembly?
1. Public order
2. Land
3. Public health
Which of the above is/are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
nf6b10dca97d.x: Public order, police and land are excluded from the Delhi Assembly's competence under Article 239AA; public health is not among them.

nc115cb7b266.s: If a State fails to comply with Union directions, which Article lets the President hold that its government cannot be carried on per the Constitution?
o: Article 356
Article 258
Article 365
Article 339
nc115cb7b266.x: Article 365 lets the President draw that conclusion when a State fails to comply with Union directions, which can open the way to action under Article 356.

nb3743ec04bb.s: Grants under Article 275 are specifically associated with:
o: discretionary grants for any public purpose
Scheduled Tribe welfare and administration of Scheduled Areas
compensation to States for GST revenue loss
urban infrastructure and metropolitan transport
nb3743ec04bb.x: Article 275 provides grants for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes and the administration of Scheduled Areas; discretionary grants for any public purpose fall under Article 282.

nc791e41f0a2.s:
Under Article 257, the Union may issue directions to a State regarding:
1. Means of communication of national or military importance
2. All matters of public order in the State
3. Protection of railways within the State
Which of the above is/are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
nc791e41f0a2.x: Article 257 covers communications of national or military importance and protection of railways; public order is not among its direction powers.

ne3819fd4e1a.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 258(2) – State entrusts its functions to the Union with the Centre's consent
Article 258A – Parliament confers duties on State officers by law without State consent
Article 258(1) – President entrusts Union functions to a State with the State's consent
Article 258(1) – Parliament confers duties on State officers by law without State consent
ne3819fd4e1a.x: Article 258(1) is Presidential entrustment of Union functions to a State with its consent; 258(2) is entrustment by Parliamentary law without consent; 258A is State-to-Union entrustment with the Centre's consent.

nbae0746b85e.s:
The Administrative Reforms Commission recommended:
1. Establishment of an Inter-State Council
2. Appointment of non-partisan Governors
3. Abolition of all advisory bodies
Which of the above is/are correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
nbae0746b85e.x: The ARC urged an Inter-State Council and non-partisan Governors; it did not recommend abolishing all advisory bodies.

nfa0bf0ed416.s: Who described the All India Services as the 'Steel Frame' of India?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru
Sardar Patel
B.R. Ambedkar
Rajendra Prasad
nfa0bf0ed416.x: Sardar Patel championed the All India Services and called them the 'Steel Frame' of India.

n00bec134a3e.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes All India Services from Central Services?
o: Central Services serve in State cadres; All India Services only in Union ministries
All India Services are confined to Union subjects; Central Services are common to Union and States
All India Services are common to Union and States; Central Services relate to Union subjects only
Both are recruited only by State Public Service Commissions
n00bec134a3e.x: All India Services are common to the Union and the States, while Central Services relate to Union subjects only.

n3c42b7d5717.s: A Joint State Public Service Commission is created by ____, and its members are appointed by ____.
o: a Presidential order; the Governor
an Act of Parliament; the President
a State law; the Chief Ministers concerned
the UPSC; the Union Home Minister
n3c42b7d5717.x: A Joint State Public Service Commission is created by an Act of Parliament, and its members are appointed by the President.

nacdae97669c.s: Zonal Councils are best described as:
o: judicial bodies whose decisions bind the States
executive bodies that allocate State finances
constitutional bodies that can dissolve State Legislatures
statutory advisory bodies whose recommendations are not binding
nacdae97669c.x: Zonal Councils are statutory, deliberative and advisory bodies; their recommendations do not bind the States.

n7068a302628.s: Which one of the following is correct about the chairmanship of the Zonal Councils?
o: The Chief Minister of the largest State chairs each council permanently
The President chairs them; the Union Home Minister is vice-chairman
The Union Home Minister chairs all five; vice-chairmanship rotates annually among member Chief Ministers
The Prime Minister chairs them; Governors are permanent vice-chairpersons
n7068a302628.x: The Union Home Minister is the common Chairman of all five Zonal Councils, and the vice-chairmanship rotates annually among the Chief Ministers of member States.

nee6b4fe7365.s: In discharging its duty under Article 355, the Union may deploy armed or central forces in a State:
o: only with the State Government's consent
with or without the State's consent
only when the State Legislature authorises it
only after a National Emergency is proclaimed
nee6b4fe7365.x: The Union may deploy armed or central forces with or without State consent in discharge of its Article 355 duty.

n1672e303f15.s: Why do States object to Union deployment of armed or central forces without their consent?
o: Public order and police are Union List subjects
Public order and police are State List subjects
Police is a Concurrent List subject
Defence is a State List subject
n1672e303f15.x: Public order and police are Entries 1 and 2 of the State List, so deployment without consent touches State authority.

nac1dfd5ce72.s: Which of the following is a power of the Union during a Financial Emergency under Article 360?
o: To dissolve State Legislatures
To directly suspend Fundamental Rights
To direct States on financial propriety and require Money Bills to be reserved for the President
To automatically assume all State legislative powers
nac1dfd5ce72.x: During a Financial Emergency, the Centre may direct States on financial propriety and require Money and Financial Bills to be reserved for the President.

nf0b7c079072.s: A surcharge levied on a tax covered by Article 270 is:
o: retained exclusively by the Union
collected and kept by the State concerned
automatically divided between the Union and States
distributed on the GST Council's recommendation
nf0b7c079072.x: Under Article 271, surcharges on Article 269 and 270 taxes are for Union purposes and are not shared with the States.

o: all Union List taxes without exception
only customs duties and Union excise duties
all State List taxes collected by the Union
Union taxes shared via the Finance Commission, excluding specified taxes, surcharges and cesses
na60e3e1bfab.x: Article 270 covers Union List taxes shared as recommended by the Finance Commission, excluding Article 268, 269 and 269A taxes, Article 271 surcharges and cesses.

nindian-polity-26-21.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 269A concerns IGST.
2. IGST is associated with the 101st Constitutional Amendment.
3. Article 270 concerns taxes shared between the Centre and the States.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
nindian-polity-26-21.x: All three are correct: Article 269A covers IGST, added by the 101st Amendment, and Article 270 covers taxes shared between the Centre and States.

n3b62b8243aa.s: Which of the following is correct about Article 131 and the Finance Commission?
o: Matters referred to the Finance Commission are excluded from Article 131
Every Finance Commission matter must be decided under Article 131
Article 131 applies only to disputes between private persons and States
Article 131 abolishes the Finance Commission's advisory role
n3b62b8243aa.x: Matters referred to the Finance Commission are excluded from Article 131, which covers original Union-State and inter-State legal disputes.

n429d3969b6d.s: Under which Article can the President modify the distribution of revenues between the Union and States during a National Emergency?
o: Article 360
Article 354
Article 280
Article 293
n429d3969b6d.x: Article 354 allows this modification until the end of the financial year in which the emergency ends. Article 360 is Financial Emergency, 280 the Finance Commission and 293 State borrowing.

nindian-polity-26-20.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 148 – Contingency Fund
Article 266 – IGST
Article 267 – Contingency Fund
Article 269A – Comptroller and Auditor General
nindian-polity-26-20.x: Article 267 covers the Contingency Fund. Article 148 is the CAG, Article 266 the Consolidated Fund and Article 269A IGST.

o: the Union Home Minister, State Home Ministers and the RBI Governor
the Finance Commission Chairman and State Chief Secretaries
the Union Finance Minister, Union Minister of State for Finance and State Finance Ministers
the Prime Minister, Union Finance Minister and all Chief Ministers
nf65e2040219.x: The GST Council comprises the Union Finance Minister (Chairperson), the Union Minister of State in charge of Finance and the State Finance Ministers.

o: are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
are meant only for Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Areas
need a Finance Commission recommendation
may be made for any public purpose
n26a59aa5e33.x: Article 282 permits discretionary grants for any public purpose; historically they were largely routed through the Planning Commission and are not charged on the Consolidated Fund.

n0a1395a8a9e.s: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended what share of the divisible pool for the States?
o: 32 percent
41 percent
42 percent
45 percent
n0a1395a8a9e.x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended 41 percent; 42 percent was the Fourteenth Finance Commission's figure.

n852095f510b.s:
Assertion (A): The Gadgil and Gadgil-Mukherjee formulas lost their earlier role in intergovernmental transfers.
Reason (R): The Planning Commission was abolished and Plan grants ended.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n852095f510b.x: Both are true, and the abolition of the Planning Commission with the end of Plan grants explains why the formulas lost their role.

o: Supreme Court to fix the borrowing limit of every State
States to guarantee Union loans without limit
Union to lend to States or guarantee their loans
Finance Commission to sanction State loans
ne14bc0fc811.x: Article 293(2) empowers the Union to make loans to States and to guarantee loans raised by them.

neb74a7087d0.s: Under Article 293(3), a State with an outstanding Union loan or guarantee needs what to raise a fresh loan?
o: Only the approval of the Reserve Bank of India
The Union's consent, which may carry conditions
The State Finance Commission's consent
No consent, if the loan is raised within India
neb74a7087d0.x: While a Union loan or guarantee is outstanding, the State needs the Union's consent for a further loan, and conditions may be attached.

n4e8c29d507a.s: Part XI of the Constitution deals with:
o: legislative and administrative relations between the Union and the States
elections and special provisions for certain classes
emergency provisions and amendment of the Constitution
financial relations and trade within India
n4e8c29d507a.x: Part XI contains legislative relations (Articles 245-255) and administrative relations (Articles 256-263) between the Union and the States.

n20948c6588d.s: During a National Emergency, India's federal structure becomes:
o: more strongly federal, with State powers protected
confederal, with States gaining international personality
quasi-unitary, with increased powers for the Union
unchanged in the legislative, executive and financial spheres
n20948c6588d.x: A National Emergency strengthens the Union, so the system operates in a unitary or quasi-unitary manner.

nindian-polity-72-19.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the IMDT Act?
o: It was enacted in 1983.
It was struck down in Sarbananda Sonowal v. Union of India (2005).
The Supreme Court held that it violated Article 355.
It was upheld as strengthening the Union's duty under Article 355.
nindian-polity-72-19.x: The IMDT Act (1983) was struck down, not upheld, in Sarbananda Sonowal (2005) for violating Article 355.

ne9dcb2003a5.s: What is the effect of Article 353 during a National Emergency?
o: State Governments are suspended and Parliament administers the States.
The Supreme Court assumes the executive functions of the States.
The Union may direct a State on any matter, but State Governments are not suspended.
The Governor alone exercises all executive power of the State.
ne9dcb2003a5.x: Article 353 enlarges the Union's executive authority to direct a State on any matter; it does not suspend State Governments.

n68b3abdb086.s: Under Article 354, during a National Emergency the President may:
o: transfer all State taxes to the Consolidated Fund of India
reduce or cancel certain transfers to States until the end of the financial year
suspend tax distribution without laying the order before Parliament
abolish the Finance Commission
n68b3abdb086.x: Article 354 lets the President modify or reduce financial transfers to States, generally until the end of the financial year; the order must be laid before Parliament.

n4b131f1cdf3.s: Article 355 imposes on the Union the duty to:
o: appoint State ministers during political instability
ensure every State follows the same economic policy
permit States to maintain their own armed forces
protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance
n4b131f1cdf3.x: Article 355 requires the Union to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance and to ensure each State is governed according to the Constitution.

n8e87dd7b26c.s: President's Rule under Article 356 has been imposed in India approximately:
o: fewer than 25 times
about 50 times
exactly 100 times
more than 125 times
n8e87dd7b26c.x: Article 356 has been used over 125 times, often against opposition-led governments, causing Centre-State friction.

na1a495c59ff.s: With cesses and surcharges excluded, the divisible pool is about what share of gross tax revenue?
na1a495c59ff.x: Excluding cesses and surcharges leaves the divisible pool at about 81% of gross tax revenue, shrinking the base shared with States.

n0fbd7652465.s: Which one of the following is correct about GST compensation to States?
o: It is guaranteed indefinitely.
It began only after the 16th Finance Commission.
It was abolished before GST commenced.
It ended in June 2022.
n0fbd7652465.x: The compensation promised to States under the GST framework ended in June 2022.

n62c297caa86.s: Which of the following are AP Reorganisation Act assurances that the opposition claims remain unmet?
o: Visakhapatnam airport, Kurnool dam and inland waterways
Kadapa steel plant, Dugarajapatnam port and metro rail
Amaravati High Court, Sriharikota port and a national university
Polavaram barrage, Hyderabad metro and a new Parliament building
n62c297caa86.x: The cited unmet assurances include the Kadapa steel plant, Dugarajapatnam port and metro rail, valued by the opposition at about Rs 5 lakh crore.

n512f3ca3f06.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First National Emergency – 1971
Second National Emergency – 1962
Third National Emergency – 25 June 1975
Second National Emergency – 25 June 1975
n512f3ca3f06.x: The first National Emergency was proclaimed in 1962, the second in 1971 and the third on 25 June 1975.

n5b1af0fbf90.s:
Consider the following about a Financial Emergency:
1. The Constitution prescribes no maximum period for it.
2. It continues until revoked.
3. It has been proclaimed several times in India.
Which of the above statements are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
n5b1af0fbf90.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; a Financial Emergency has never been declared in India.

nindian-polity-44-9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about parliamentary approval of emergencies?
o: A National Emergency must be approved within one month.
President's Rule must be approved within one month.
A Financial Emergency must be approved within two months.
The 44th Amendment, 1978 cut the National Emergency period from two months to one.
nindian-polity-44-9.x: President's Rule must be approved within two months, like a Financial Emergency; only a National Emergency has one month.

nindian-polity-44-14.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Vice-President acts as President when the President's office falls vacant due to death, resignation or removal.
2. Such a vacancy must be filled within six months.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
nindian-polity-44-14.x: Both are true: the Vice-President acts as President until a new President is elected, which must happen within six months.

n58769ea75a4.s: Both the emergency provisions and the ordinance power of the Indian Constitution are drawn from the:
o: Government of India Act, 1919
Weimar Constitution
Government of India Act, 1935
Charter Act, 1833
n58769ea75a4.x: The emergency provisions and the ordinance power (Articles 123 and 213) are relics of the Government of India Act, 1935; the Weimar Constitution is the source of suspending Fundamental Rights in an emergency.

n56805b534fd.s: Which amendment ensured that an order under Article 359 cannot suspend the enforcement of Articles 20 and 21?
o: 38th Amendment, 1975
42nd Amendment, 1976
43rd Amendment, 1977
44th Amendment, 1978
n56805b534fd.x: The 44th Amendment, 1978 protected Articles 20 and 21 from suspension under Article 359, even during a National Emergency.

nindian-polity-50-11.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 359 suspends the right to approach courts to enforce specified Fundamental Rights.
2. Article 359 operates only during an external emergency and not during armed rebellion.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
nindian-polity-50-11.x: Statement 1 is true; statement 2 is false because Article 359 applies in external emergencies and in armed rebellion.

n147edb5dde1.s: Which one of the following is correct about the National Emergency of 25 June 1975?
o: It was proclaimed by the Union Cabinet on the ground of armed rebellion.
It was proclaimed by President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed on the ground of internal disturbance.
It was proclaimed by the President on the ground of external aggression.
It was proclaimed after the 44th Amendment on the ground of internal disturbance.
n147edb5dde1.x: President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed proclaimed the Emergency on 25 June 1975 on the ground of internal disturbance.

n803aab89e11.s: In S.R. Bommai v. Union of India, the Supreme Court recognised which as basic features of the Constitution?
o: Secularism and parliamentary sovereignty
Federalism and the Governor's discretion
Secularism and federalism
Federalism and single citizenship
n803aab89e11.x: The Bommai judgment recognised secularism and federalism as basic features of the Constitution.

n6a6045cfd4a.s: In December 2020, the AP High Court asked whether it could record a breakdown of constitutional machinery in the State. This relates to:
o: Article 352
Article 360
Article 356
Article 365
n6a6045cfd4a.x: A breakdown of constitutional machinery in a State is the ground for President's Rule under Article 356.

nindian-polity-15-21.s:
Assertion (A): Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights but cannot destroy the Basic Structure of the Constitution.
Reason (R): The Basic Structure principle was laid down in Kesavananda Bharati (1973).
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nindian-polity-15-21.x: Both are true and R explains A: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held that Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights but not the basic structure.

nf522e4e7d6c.s: The Inter-State Council under Article 263 is:
o: a judicial body whose awards bind like Supreme Court judgments
an extra-constitutional body created by executive resolution
a recommendatory body whose decisions legally bind all States
a recommendatory body for consultation on inter-governmental matters
nf522e4e7d6c.x: The Inter-State Council is a constitutional, recommendatory body under Article 263; it is neither judicial nor created by mere executive resolution.

nbb830ae68a7.s: The Inter-State Council under Article 263 was set up in 1990 on the recommendation of the:
o: Sarkaria Commission
Rajamannar Committee
Administrative Reforms Commission
Punchhi Commission
nbb830ae68a7.x: The Council was established in 1990 following the Sarkaria Commission; the ARC and Rajamannar Committee had earlier supported it, and Punchhi came later.

nb6a03bc73be.s:
Consider the following about the Zonal Councils:
1. Chief Ministers act as Vice-Chairmen by annual rotation.
2. Their recommendations are legally binding on the States.
3. They are deliberative and advisory bodies.
Which of the above statements are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
nb6a03bc73be.x: Chief Ministers rotate annually as Vice-Chairmen and the Councils are advisory; their recommendations are not binding.

n4379f9487ff.s: At the January 2026 CWC-chaired inter-State meeting, Andhra Pradesh said Telangana's 50:50 Krishna water demand:
o: should be accepted immediately
is contrary to the KWDT awards and Apex Council decisions
should be settled jointly through the Zonal Council
should be referred to the Supreme Court
n4379f9487ff.x: Andhra Pradesh rejected the 50:50 demand as contrary to the KWDT awards and the Apex Council's decisions.

n54f7b5e46a8.s: A principal argument for greater State autonomy is that States:
o: lack adequate resources for the duties assigned to them
have surplus revenue beyond their needs
have no role in delivering public services
need closer central supervision
n54f7b5e46a8.x: A major argument for State autonomy is that States often lack sufficient resources to perform their constitutionally assigned duties.

n2f5ae442ebd.s: On residuary powers, the Sarkaria Commission proposed that:
o: all residuary powers go to the States
residuary taxation stay with Parliament and other residuary matters go to the Concurrent List
all residuary powers, including taxation, go to the Concurrent List
all residuary powers remain exclusively with Parliament
n2f5ae442ebd.x: Sarkaria proposed keeping residuary taxation with Parliament and placing the remaining residuary matters in the Concurrent List.

n25c03cd1fe8.s: In the federal context, the Planning Commission was criticised as:
o: a statutory body collecting taxes on behalf of States
an extra-constitutional body that made States dependent on the Union for aid
a judicial body adjudicating disputes between States
a constitutional body controlling State Legislatures
n25c03cd1fe8.x: Critics called the Planning Commission an extra-constitutional institution that made States 'suppliants for aid'.

n54442f735ff.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Rajamannar Committee – Tamil Nadu
2. Anandpur Sahib Resolution – Punjab
3. Formal autonomy demand – Kerala
Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
n54442f735ff.x: The Rajamannar Committee belongs to Tamil Nadu and the Anandpur Sahib Resolution to Punjab; Kerala had no formal autonomy demand in this context.

n941388c9131.s:
Consider the following about the Rajamannar Committee:
1. It was appointed by the Tamil Nadu Government.
2. It had three members.
3. Its recommendations were accepted by the Union Government.
Which of the above statements are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
n941388c9131.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the Centre ignored the committee's recommendations.

ne3ddd23e46b.s:
Which of the following were recommended by the Administrative Reforms Commission?
1. An Inter-State Council under Article 263
2. Non-partisan Governors
3. Complete deletion of Article 356
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
ne3ddd23e46b.x: The ARC recommended an Inter-State Council and non-partisan Governors; deleting Article 356 was the Rajamannar Committee's demand.

n6bb53fa874e.s: If a State withdraws general consent to the CBI, then:
o: its cases pass automatically to the NIA
the CBI is permanently barred from all cases in the State
the CBI must obtain consent case by case
the CBI may investigate on Union direction without approval
n6bb53fa874e.x: Withdrawal of general consent means the CBI must seek the State's consent separately for each case.

n6332c8eb824.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 371A – Sikkim
Article 371D – Central University in Andhra Pradesh
Article 371E – Central University in Andhra Pradesh
Article 371F – Nagaland
n6332c8eb824.x: Article 371E concerns a Central University in Andhra Pradesh; 371A is Nagaland, 371D local cadres, education and jobs in AP, and 371F Sikkim.

n41fe2d98580.s: State autonomy demands in India have mainly sought:
o: a uniform language policy for all States
transfer of defence and foreign affairs to local bodies
more powers, greater own revenue and less central administrative control
abolition of State legislatures and central taxation
n41fe2d98580.x: Autonomy demands sought more powers for States, more control over own revenue and reduced central administrative control.

n914a42bb187.s: The defeat of the 131st Amendment Bill, 2026 on Lok Sabha expansion sharpened which debate?
o: The North–South debate
The judicial appointments debate
The GST compensation debate
The debate on abolishing local governments
n914a42bb187.x: The defeat of the 131st Amendment Bill on Lok Sabha expansion sharpened the North–South debate.

n169fd2814c0.s:
Consider the following about the Inter-State Council:
1. It was set up in 1990 under Article 263 on the Sarkaria Commission's advice.
2. It is chaired by the Union Home Minister.
3. Its 11th meeting was held on 16 July 2016.
Which of the above statements are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
n169fd2814c0.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; the Prime Minister chairs the Council, while the Home Minister chairs its Standing Committee.

n9ea65602ba5.s: Which one of the following explains fiscal centralisation after GST?
o: GST abolished the divisible pool of Union taxes.
GST subsumed several State taxes, while cesses and surcharges stayed outside the divisible pool.
Cesses and surcharges automatically joined the divisible pool.
State taxes expanded and all cesses entered the divisible pool.
n9ea65602ba5.x: GST subsumed several State taxes, while cesses and surcharges remain outside the divisible pool.

n65d366a99e3.s: The Rajamannar Committee is significant as the:
o: first Union-appointed commission on Centre-State relations
first committee on Centre-State relations appointed by a State
first committee to recommend abolishing the Finance Commission
first committee formed after the Inter-State Council was set up
n65d366a99e3.x: The Rajamannar Committee was the first committee on Centre-State relations appointed by a State.

n9b6fa5f63dc.s: On residuary powers, the Rajamannar Committee and the Sarkaria Commission respectively favoured:
o: Concurrent List; the States
local bodies; the Union
the States; the Concurrent List for non-tax residuary matters
the Union; the Union
n9b6fa5f63dc.x: Rajamannar wanted residuary powers given to the States; Sarkaria placed residuary powers other than taxation in the Concurrent List.

n49b2faca5c0.s: The Inter-State Council was established in 1990 through the influence of the:
o: Rajamannar Committee
Punchhi Commission
Kurian Joseph Committee
Sarkaria Commission
n49b2faca5c0.x: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 through the Sarkaria Commission's influence.

nbf1c90d3a5d.s: Besides the Rajamannar Committee, P.V. Rajamannar also chaired the:
o: First Finance Commission
Third Finance Commission
Fourth Finance Commission
Fifth Finance Commission
nbf1c90d3a5d.x: P.V. Rajamannar chaired both the Rajamannar Committee and the Fourth Finance Commission.

n7e0248ceb48.s:
Consider the following about the Sarkaria Commission:
1. It was to suggest changes in Centre-State relations within the existing constitutional framework.
2. It submitted its report in 1988.
3. It was appointed by the Government of Tamil Nadu.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
n7e0248ceb48.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the Central Government, not Tamil Nadu, set up the Commission in June 1983.

n297e9d3341c.s: The Inter-State Council of 1990 implemented which Sarkaria recommendation?
o: Abolition of All-India Services
A permanent intergovernmental forum under Article 263
Transfer of residuary taxation to the States
Mandatory dissolution of Assemblies under Article 356
n297e9d3341c.x: The Inter-State Council, set up in 1990 under Article 263, is regarded as the main implemented Sarkaria recommendation.

ne89e13f9852.s: On All-India Services, Sarkaria and Rajamannar respectively recommended:
o: strengthening them; abolishing them
abolishing them; strengthening them
abolishing them; abolishing them
transferring them to local governments; abolishing them
ne89e13f9852.x: Sarkaria wanted All-India Services strengthened and more of them created, whereas Rajamannar wanted them abolished.

n0495fde7411.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Sarkaria – abolition of All-India Services
Rajamannar – a strong Centre
Punchhi – localised emergency and fixed tenure for Governors
Punchhi – opposition to fixed tenure for Governors
n0495fde7411.x: Punchhi proposed localised emergency and fixed tenure for Governors; Sarkaria strengthened All-India Services and Rajamannar sought State autonomy.

n344ee6e2a25.s:
Consider the following about the Punchhi Commission:
1. It was formally called the Commission on Centre-State Relations.
2. It was appointed by a State Government.
3. It submitted its report in 2010.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
n344ee6e2a25.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; the Commission was appointed by the Government of India, not a State.

ncd241793086.s: The Punchhi Commission recommended that a Governor's tenure should be:
o: rotated among States every two years
limited to three years by Parliament
a fixed five years, insulated from Central pressure
at the pleasure of the Union Cabinet
ncd241793086.x: Punchhi recommended a fixed five-year tenure so that Governors are insulated from Central pressure.

nfcce7a52f4e.s: On State universities, the Punchhi Commission recommended that Governors:
o: be Chancellors only during President's Rule
appoint Vice-Chancellors without State involvement
compulsorily remain Chancellors of all State universities
not be made Chancellors or given other statutory university roles
nfcce7a52f4e.x: To avoid clashes with State Governments, Punchhi recommended that Governors not be made Chancellors or given statutory university roles.

n60b609bfe11.s:
Consider the following Punchhi Commission recommendations on removing a Governor:
1. Delete 'during the pleasure of the President' from Article 156.
2. Remove a Governor only by impeachment by the State Legislature, like the President.
3. Rotate Governors among States periodically.
Which of the above is/are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
n60b609bfe11.x: Punchhi wanted the pleasure clause removed and impeachment-style removal; periodic rotation of Governors was not its recommendation.

n4f2272e1737.s: On Articles 355 and 356, the Punchhi Commission recommended that:
o: they be retained unamended and used freely
they be amended, with Article 356 used sparingly as a last resort
Article 356 be the normal remedy for State political disputes
both be repealed immediately
n4f2272e1737.x: Punchhi recommended amending Articles 355 and 356 and using Article 356 sparingly, only as a last resort and never in a partisan manner.

n2c75b74f3c0.s:
Consider the following recommendations:
1. The National Integration Council should meet at least once a year.
2. The Prime Minister and Chief Ministers should meet regularly to promote cooperation.
3. The Inter-State Council should meet once in two years.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
n2c75b74f3c0.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the Inter-State Council was recommended to meet at least thrice a year.

nec4af006e62.s: A 'localised emergency' under Articles 355 and 356 would let the Centre:
o: take over the whole country indefinitely
take over a district or part of a district for a limited period
permanently suspend local governments in the State
dissolve every State Legislature during public disorder
nec4af006e62.x: A localised emergency would let the Centre take over a specific troubled area, such as a district, for a limited period instead of the whole State.

n73a8ac3b52c.s: Which one of the following is correct about judicial rulings on Governors' timelines for Bills?
o: The 8 April 2025 Tamil Nadu case let Governors withhold assent indefinitely.
The 2025 Presidential Reference abolished judicial review of Governors.
The 8 April 2025 Tamil Nadu case fixed timelines, but the 20 November 2025 Presidential Reference held courts cannot impose fixed timelines or deemed assent.
The 2025 Presidential Reference made deemed assent mandatory.
n73a8ac3b52c.x: The Tamil Nadu case (8 April 2025) fixed timelines, but the Presidential Reference opinion (20 November 2025) held that courts cannot impose fixed timelines or deemed assent.

n0172801c3b0.s:
Consider the following about the Second Administrative Reforms Commission:
1. It was chaired first by M. Veerappa Moily and later by V. Ramachandran.
2. It submitted 15 reports between 2006 and 2009.
3. It was constituted in 1966.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
n0172801c3b0.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the Second ARC was constituted in 2005, while 1966 is the first ARC.

nf570d889e0c.s: The Bhagwan Sahay Committee of Governors described the Governor as:
o: the Union's political agent in the State
only the State's executive head, with no Union role
the presiding officer of the State Legislature
both the State's constitutional head and a link with the Centre
nf570d889e0c.x: The Committee saw the Governor as both the State's constitutional head and a link with the Centre, keeping watch and reporting to the Centre.

nindian-society-11-15.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Liberhan Commission was chaired by M.S. Liberhan.
2. It inquired into the Babri Masjid demolition.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
nindian-society-11-15.x: Both are true: Justice M.S. Liberhan chaired the commission on the 1992 Babri Masjid demolition.

na0345b3a265.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Sarkaria Commission
2. First ARC study team report
3. Punchhi Commission
4. Setting up of the Inter-State Council
na0345b3a265.x: First ARC study team (1969), Sarkaria Commission (1983-88), Inter-State Council (1990), Punchhi Commission (2007-10).

n60b859048a1.s: The GST Council and NITI Aayog's State rankings are usually cited, respectively, as examples of:
o: competitive and cooperative federalism
cooperative and competitive federalism
competitive federalism in both cases
cooperative federalism in both cases
n60b859048a1.x: The GST Council is a model of cooperative federalism, whereas NITI Aayog rankings promote competitive federalism.

n063263db869.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Planning Commission – Executive resolution, 1952
National Development Council – Cabinet resolution, 1950
NITI Aayog – Union Cabinet resolution, 1 January 2015
Planning Commission – Union Cabinet resolution, 1 January 2015
n063263db869.x: NITI Aayog was created by a Union Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015; the Planning Commission by a Cabinet resolution in 1950 and the NDC by an executive resolution in 1952.

nindian-polity-65-1.s: A Constitutional Body is one that is:
o: created by an Act of Parliament
created by an executive order
directly established by the Constitution
created by a State Legislature alone
nindian-polity-65-1.x: A constitutional body is set up and empowered by the Constitution itself, such as the ECI or the CAG; bodies created by law are statutory.

nindian-polity-65-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: NITI Aayog was set up by a Cabinet resolution in 2015.
The National Development Council was set up by an executive order in 1952.
The Planning Commission was a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament.
The Planning Commission was set up by a Cabinet resolution in 1950.
nindian-polity-65-2.x: The Planning Commission (1950) was created by a Cabinet resolution, so it was extra-constitutional and non-statutory.

nindian-polity-65-3.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A statutory body is created by an Act of Parliament or a State Legislature.
2. The NHRC, Lokpal and NGT are statutory bodies.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
nindian-polity-65-3.x: Both are true: statutory bodies are created by legislation, and the NHRC, Lokpal and NGT are examples.

n2a205eb5132.s:
Consider the following about the GST Council:
1. It is provided for in Article 279A.
2. The Centre has two-thirds of the votes and the States together one-third.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
n2a205eb5132.x: Article 279A provides for the GST Council; the voting share is the reverse, with the Centre holding one-third and the States two-thirds.

n3b6b0d14ded.s:
Consider the following sub-groups of Chief Ministers and their convenors:
1. Rationalisation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes – Shivraj Singh Chouhan
2. Skill Development – Parkash Singh Badal
3. Swachh Bharat Abhiyan – N. Chandrababu Naidu
Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
n3b6b0d14ded.x: All three are correct: Chouhan, Badal and Naidu convened the respective sub-groups.

n2ea872d3f21.s: In the SDG India Index 2023-24, Andhra Pradesh's score and category were:
o: 100 out of 100; Front Runner
74 out of 100; Frontrunner
57 out of 100; Aspirant
74 out of 100; Performer
n2ea872d3f21.x: Andhra Pradesh scored 74 out of 100 and was classified as a Frontrunner.
